claim.text: Complexity regularization that satisfies Norton's Material Theory of Induction (MTI) by localizing the inductive risk to local facts in the given domain — exemplified by the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis (LTH) and its iterative magnitude pruning (IMP) — provides an epistemic justification for inductive generalizations learned by overparameterized artificial neural networks. Unlike global uniformities such as simplicity or compression, MTI-based regularization avoids epistemic circularity because the inductive risk is transferred from a generic schema to the actual local facts present in the training data, making the resulting generalization epistemically justifiable without appealing to non-local facts.
For overparameterized neural networks, Empirical Risk Minimization (ERM) can suffer from a No-Go-ERM trivialization (claim 3, claim 5).
For overparameterized neural networks, the two-sided uniform convergence of empirical risk to risk fails.

For overparameterized neural networks, both data-distribution-independent bounds (based on Vapnik-Chervonenkis (VC) dimension) and data-distribution-dependent bounds (based on weight norms) become uninformative.
That the two-sided uniform convergence of empirical risk to risk fails results in the absence of asymptotic stability of Empirical Risk Minimization (ERM).

For overparameterized neural networks, the collapse of Empirical Risk Minimization (ERM) to trivialization can be blocked by adopting a local stability provided by the Material Theory of Induction (MTI).
The strengths of inductive support for Empirical Risk Minimization (ERM) are derived from the local context rather than from a global asymptotic requirement.

For overparameterized neural networks, the Material Theory of Induction (MTI) replaces the unavailable asymptotic uniform convergence of empirical risk to risk with a strictly local convergence of empirical risk to risk.

For overparameterized neural networks, local stability of Empirical Risk Minimization under the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis is achieved when iterative magnitude pruning identifies matching subnetworks (as defined in note 1, note 2, note 3, note 4) that are robust to stochastic gradient descent noise.
Robustness to stochastic gradient descent (SGD) noise is characterized by linear mode connectivity (see note 5, note 6).

At each round \(n\) of iterative magnitude pruning (IMP), if the axial subspace defined by the refined pruning mask \(m_{n+1}\) (see note 7) intersects the epsilon-linearly connected sublevel set (LCSS; see note 8) of the current weights \(W_n\), then rewinding the remaining weights to their values at an early training step \(k\) (obtaining \(W_k\)) and training the subnetwork \(f(X; m_{n+1} \odot W_k)\) to convergence produces updated weights \(W_{n+1}\) that are linearly mode-connected to \(W_n\) (see note 5, note 6) and have test error within \(\epsilon\) of the original dense network \(f(X; W)\).
The geometric condition in claim 11 is necessary and sufficient for iterative magnitude pruning (IMP) to find a matching subnetwork (as defined in note 1, note 2, note 3, note 4) at round \(n\).
The geometric condition in claim 11 provides the local stability that de-trivializes Empirical Risk Minimization (ERM).

The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis has been empirically confirmed for neural network architectures used in natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning, as well as for pre-trained models.

Winning subnetworks (sparse subnetworks that, when their weights are reset to their initial values, can be trained to match the test accuracy of the original dense network) or matching subnetworks (sparse subnetworks found by iterative magnitude pruning with weight rewinding that achieve test accuracy within a small tolerance of the dense network) were successfully identified in the neural network architectures used in natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning, as well as for pre-trained models.

Pruning based on the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis localizes inductive risk by adapting the network's structure to local facts in each domain—natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning—as well as for pre-trained models.

Pruning based on the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis validates the Material Theory of Induction framework across different contexts—natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning—as well as for pre-trained models.

The epistemic justification provided by Material Theory of Induction -based complexity regularization holds only when the training data are independent and identically distributed from a fixed distribution and the local facts remain stable across the training and deployment domains.

If these conditions—that the training data are independent and identically distributed from a fixed distribution and that the local facts remain stable across the training and deployment domains—are violated, the Material Theory of Induction (MTI) justification fails.

If these conditions—that the training data are independent and identically distributed from a fixed distribution and that the local facts remain stable across the training and deployment domains—are violated, the inductive risk must be managed by a different type of justification from the Material Theory of Induction (MTI) justification—specifically, optimality-based meta-induction.
Optimality-based meta-induction does not require assumptions about data uniformity.
In machine learning, there is a division of labor.
The Material Theory of Induction (MTI) provides local justification when data are stationary.
Optimality-based meta-induction justifications provide global justification for model selection under non-stationary conditions.
The strengths of inductive support for Empirical Risk Minimization (ERM) are derived from a winning ticket rather than from a global asymptotic requirement.
Under distribution shifts, the Material Theory of Induction (MTI) justification fails.

note.text: elaboration of matching sparse subnetwork: a subnetwork \(f(X; m \odot W)\) produced by applying pruning mask \(m\)
elaboration of pruning mask \(m\): (a binary vector indicating which weights are retained)
elaboration of matching sparse subnetwork: such that its test error \(\mathcal{E}(m \odot W) \leq \mathcal{E}(W) + \epsilon\).
two sets of network weights are linearly mode-connected if
elaboration of linearly mode-connected: they are connected in weight space by a line along which test error does not increase.
elaboration of axial subspace defined by the refined pruning mask \(m_{n+1}\): (i.e., the subspace of weight space where components corresponding to pruned weights are zero)

elaboration of epsilon-linearly connected sublevel set: the set of all weight vectors \(W'\) whose test error \(\mathcal{E}(W')\) is within \(\epsilon\) of \(\mathcal{E}(W)\) and which are linearly mode-connected to \(W\).
